extracted.intended_audience: parties and counsel participating in Copyright Claims Board (CCB) proceedings (claimants, respondents, and their representatives)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and substantive submission standards for filings, discovery, testimony, hearings, settlement, protective orders, and evidence before the Copyright Claims Board (CCB). Targets how to prepare and file requests, written testimony, and related materials and how the Board will manage proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory eCCB submission for listed requests and responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents listed under the specified subsection shall be submitted through a fillable form on eCCB and shall comply with the following requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All requests and responses identified in the tier lists must use the eCCB fillable form (subject to the tier-specific character/page limits and attachment rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier one requests and responses — format, limits, and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Tier one requests and responses must be filed through the fillable form on eCCB and be limited to 4,000 characters. Any party may submit a response within seven days of the filing of the request. The Board may deny such a request before the time to submit a response expires, but will not grant a request before the response time expires unless consented to by all parties. No replies from a party that submits a request, absent leave of the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tier one submissions include a fixed set of request types (e.g., requests to amend scheduling order; general or discovery conferences not involving a dispute; statements as to damages; requests for hearings; withdrawal of claims; settlement conferences; stays for settlement; joint requests for dismissal; standard or custom protective orders; removing confidentiality designations; use of not previously submitted evidence at a hearing; modify discovery schedule; withhold privileged documents; notices regarding missed deadlines; requests to designate an official reporter; requests to withdraw representation; other requests covered under §220.5(d)). Parties should ensure Tier one requests fall within these categories and meet the 4,000-character limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier two requests and responses — format, limits, and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Tier two requests and responses must be filed through the fillable form on eCCB and be limited to 10,000 characters (not including permitted attachments). Any party may file a response within 14 days of the filing of the request or the order to show cause. The Board may deny before the response time expires but will not grant before the response time expires unless consented to by all parties. No replies from a party that submits a request, absent leave of the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tier two includes more substantive or potentially impactful requests (e.g., amending pleadings; consolidation; intervention; dismissal for unsuitability; additional discovery requests — which must list each specific interrogatory/document/request for admission sought; responses to such discovery requests; serving requests for admission; presenting an expert witness; conferences to resolve discovery disputes — which must attach inadequate responses; requests for sanctions; requests for third-party attendance at hearings; and requests/responses related to alleged or patterned bad-faith conduct). Follow the 10,000-character limit and include required attachments where specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier three — uploaded written submissions and general formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the Board orders otherwise, written submissions not identified as tier one or tier two shall be uploaded to eCCB, comply with applicable page limitations and response times, and shall include: a title; a caption; be typewritten; be double-spaced (except headings, footnotes, or block quotations); be in 12-point type or larger; and include the typed or handwritten signature of the submitting party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement statements under §222.18(d) are an exception to eCCB filing. Ensure submissions observe the page and response-time limits set elsewhere in the subchapter and the formatting rules above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier three — examples of documents treated as tier three submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents considered tier three include direct party statements and response party statements; reply party statements; settlement position statements; requests to reconsider determinations to dismiss for unsuitability; smaller claims position statements; responses to smaller claims Board-proposed findings of fact; claimant written direct party statement in support of default; claimant response to Board determination after default that evidence is insufficient; response to notice of proposed default determination; requests to vacate a default determination; request to vacate a dismissal for failure to prosecute; requests for reconsideration and responses; requests for review by the Register of Copyrights and responses thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These enumerated submission types must be uploaded and comply with tier three formatting and any applicable page limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Other than written testimony submitted pursuant to §222.15, replies to any responses to requests or written submissions shall not be permitted, unless otherwise provided for in this subchapter or permitted by the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not file reply briefs/responses unless the subchapter explicitly allows or the Board grants leave.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other (non-enumerated) requests procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any requests to the Board not specified in this part can be submitted by filing a request not otherwise covered under paragraph (a)(1). Depending on the nature of the request, the Board will advise whether the request is permitted and, if so, when a response must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a request doesn't fit a listed tier category, submit it as 'request not otherwise covered' and await Board guidance on whether it is permitted and the timing for responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Federal Rules of Civil Procedure and Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board is not bound by the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure or the Federal Rules of Evidence; the rules governing CCB proceedings are set forth in the subchapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume FRCP or FRE control; follow the Board's procedural and evidentiary rules as specified in this subchapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial and second notice requirements for smaller claims proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If the claimant has requested that the proceeding be conducted as a smaller claim under 37 CFR part 226, the initial notice and second notice must include a statement that the proceeding shall be conducted as a smaller claim and a brief explanation of the differences between smaller claims proceedings and other Board proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure notices to respondents clearly state when smaller-claims procedures are sought and provide a concise explanation of how smaller claims differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to file a response or counterclaim response (default)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to file a response or a counterclaim response within the required timeframe may constitute a default under 17 U.S.C. 1506(u), and the Board may begin default proceedings under part 227 of this subchapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely filing of responses and counterclaim responses is critical to avoid default proceedings; track deadlines carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling order issuance and content
rubrics_metrics.description: After receipt of the second payment of the filing fee and completion of the 14-day period specified in the Board's order, the Board shall issue an initial scheduling order through eCCB. The scheduling order shall include dates/deadlines for: filing respondent's response; a pre-discovery conference; service of responses to standard interrogatories; service of documents responsive to standard production requests; requests for leave to seek additional discovery; close of discovery; a post-discovery conference; and filing of each party's written testimony and responses pursuant to §222.15.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect the scheduling order to set the core case-management deadlines and to provide deadlines for submission of standard discovery and testimony. All conferences shall be held virtually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board-held conferences and virtual format
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to identified conferences, the Board may hold additional conferences at its election or at the request of any party. All conferences shall be held virtually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for conferences must follow §220.5(a)(1) and use virtual platforms as directed by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amending the scheduling order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may amend the initial scheduling order upon clearance of a counterclaim, upon request by parties to an active proceeding submitted through eCCB, as necessary to adjust dates for conferences/hearings/stays, to facilitate settlement, or on its own initiative to maintain orderly administration of the docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to amend follow §220.5(a)(1). The Board will consider counterclaim clearance, case activity, settlement needs, and docket administration in amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to pleadings — when allowed and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Claimants notified that a claim does not comply may freely amend as part of an amended claim; claimants whose claim was found compliant may freely amend once as a matter of course prior to service; counterclaimants may freely amend once prior to the response; otherwise, amendments require Board leave. Amending a pleading may trigger compliance review under §224.1(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for leave to amend must set forth reasons and follow §220.5(a)(2). Standard for granting leave: the Board grants leave if justice so requires after considering prejudice to other parties (including impact on opt-out rights), undue delay, and whether the amendment basis should have been known earlier; if granted, leave applies only to specific amendments requested. Time to respond to an amended pleading is the remaining time to respond to the original pleading or within 30 days after notification the amended pleading is compliant, whichever is later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation — when allowed and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: If a claimant has multiple active proceedings against the same respondent or arising out of the same facts/circumstances, the Board may consolidate proceedings for discovery, evidence submission, or hearings. Consolidated proceedings remain separate for determinations and damages awards. The Board may consolidate at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The party seeking consolidation must submit a request setting reasons, request a conference with parties from each affected case, and provide docket numbers; requests follow §220.5(a)(2). The Board balances need/benefit of consolidation against timeliness and potential prejudice from delay in making the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessary party standard and joinder/intervention procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A necessary party is one whose absence would prevent the Board from according complete relief, would impair the party's ability to protect an interest, or whose absence creates a substantial risk of inconsistent obligations. Any party who believes a necessary party is missing may file a request; if the Board finds a necessary party missing, it shall dismiss the proceeding without prejudice as unsuitable for CCB proceedings. Third parties may request to intervene as necessary parties following §220.5(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Board determines an intervenor is not necessary, it will deny the request and resume proceedings unless all parties agree to join the party. If necessary and no party opposed, the intervenor may join; if opposed, the Board may dismiss without prejudice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for written testimony on the merits
rubrics_metrics.description: After the close of discovery and by times specified in the scheduling order, parties asserting claims or counterclaims shall file written direct testimony. Parties responding must file written response testimony within 45 days of service of written direct testimony. Parties who asserted a claim or counterclaim may file written reply testimony within 21 days after service of written response testimony. All written testimony must be uploaded to eCCB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe the 45-day and 21-day timelines; ensure timely eCCB uploading in accordance with the scheduling order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of written direct and response testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Written direct and response testimony shall consist of documentary evidence and a party statement, and may include witness statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentary evidence must be accompanied by a statement listing each submitted document and a brief description of how it bears on the claim or counterclaim. Direct/response documentary evidence may only include documents served on opposing parties pursuant to the scheduling order, absent leave for good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witness statements requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A witness statement must be sworn under penalty of perjury; be detailed as to the substance of the witness's knowledge and organized into numbered paragraphs; and contain only factual information based on the witness's personal knowledge and not legal argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure witness statements are properly sworn, carefully organized, limited to personal-knowledge facts, and avoid legal conclusions or argumentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Party statement content and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A party statement shall set forth the party's position as to key facts and damages and any position as to the law; need not include a table of contents or authorities; shall be limited to 12 pages (other than optional table of contents or authorities) and must meet §220.5(b) requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For claimants seeking damages, include whether electing statutory or actual damages and any profits (election may be changed up until final determination). For respondents, the party statement may include whether, if found liable, the party would voluntarily agree to an order to cease or mitigate unlawful activity — election must be made by filing of the party statement or at a hearing and may be considered only for damages, not liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply testimony — scope and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Written reply testimony must be limited to addressing or rebutting specific evidence in written response testimony. Reply documentary evidence limited to that required to contradict/rebut specific evidence and shall not include any documentary evidence previously presented as part of the submitting party's direct testimony. Reply witness statements limited to new facts that contradict or rebut specific response testimony. A reply party statement must be limited to rebutting/addressing opposing response testimony, may not include discussion of facts, law, or damages that was included in the party's direct party statement, must meet §220.5(b), and is limited to seven pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use reply testimony to rehash direct testimony or to introduce broad new claims; strictly limit reply materials to rebuttal of specific response evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of written testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: All written testimony submitted to the Board must include a certification by the submitting party that it is accurate and truthful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an explicit certification statement attesting to the accuracy and truthfulness of the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for hearings on the merits — timing and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party may include a request for a hearing on the merits in a party statement or submit following §220.5(a)(1) no later than 7 days after the date by which reply testimony may be submitted. The Board has sole discretion to hold a hearing. Any request in a party statement should consist of a short statement providing reasons why the request should be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File hearing requests promptly and succinctly; the Board may elect to hold a hearing even without a party request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearings — virtual format, recording, scheduling, and close of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: All hearings shall be held virtually and may be recorded. When the Board determines a hearing is appropriate, it will issue an amended scheduling order setting the hearing date and deadlines for additional evidence or a pre-hearing conference. Following a hearing, no additional written testimony or evidence may be submitted unless requested by the Board or with leave for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare for virtual hearings, possible recording, and strict close-of-evidence rules limiting post-hearing filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of claims and dismissal procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may request to withdraw its own claim or counterclaim by filing a brief written request. If received before a response is filed, the Board shall dismiss without prejudice unless parties agree in writing to dismissal with prejudice. If after a response, the Board shall issue a final determination dismissing with prejudice unless the Board determines in the interests of justice to dismiss without prejudice or all parties agree to dismissal without prejudice. Dismissal under this section will not affect remaining claims or counterclaims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal timing relative to responses determines whether dismissal is with or without prejudice; obtain written stipulations if different treatment is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement facilitation and settlement conference procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board shall facilitate voluntary settlement and will raise settlement conferences at pre- and post-discovery conferences. At any point in an active proceeding parties may jointly request a settlement conference. Requests may be oral at a Board conference or in writing and may include a request to stay proceedings while settlement discussions occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a joint request or no party response within 7 days, the Board will schedule a settlement conference with all parties; if objections are filed, the Board may schedule with some or all parties based on likely resolution. Requests follow §220.5(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement position statements — form, timing, and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Three days prior to a settlement conference, each participating party must submit a position statement to the presiding Officer by email and, when agreed, send it to other participating parties outside eCCB. The position statement shall not exceed five pages and attach no more than 20 pages of exhibits (absent leave), and shall meet §220.5(b) requirements. The statement must set forth a brief overview of facts and contentions; the relief sought including damages amount; whether the alleged wrongful conduct is currently taking place; and any prior attempts at resolution including offers or counteroffers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement statements are not filed on eCCB; keep them concise, include essential factual and settlement posture information, and attach only necessary exhibits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recusal of presiding Officer for settlement conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: The Officer presiding over the settlement conference shall not participate in rendering the determination in the proceeding unless other Officers cannot reach consensus. The presiding Officer may review the record and attend any hearing but shall not actively participate in hearing or substantive Officer discussions concerning the proceeding or determination, except when other Officers cannot reach consensus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect the presiding settlement Officer to be insulated from final determinations except in rare circumstances of non-consensus among other Officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay of proceeding for settlement discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may stay the proceeding for 30 days concurrently with scheduling a settlement conference, at the time of or following the conference, or at the request of the parties. Parties may request an extension of the stay in good faith. If settlement is not reached when the stay/extension expires, the Board will issue an amended scheduling order to govern the remainder of the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use stays to facilitate settlement but be prepared for the Board to resume scheduling if settlement is not achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of settlement agreement and Board adoption of terms
rubrics_metrics.description: If parties reach a settlement they may submit a joint request to dismiss claims and may request the Board adopt some or all settlement terms in its final determination. The Board shall dismiss claims with prejudice unless parties request without prejudice. The Board may incorporate settlement terms into its final determination unless it finds them clearly unconscionable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When seeking Board adoption of settlement terms, ensure terms are not unconscionable and clearly drafted for possible incorporation into a final determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard protective order — scope and use
rubrics_metrics.description: At a party's request the Board's standard protective order will govern discovery material exchanged to protect against improper use or disclosure. Discovery material received from another party may be used only in connection with the proceeding, and all copies must be returned or disposed of within 30 days of a determination or dismissal or within 30 days of exhaustion of review/appeal time, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for a standard protective order follow §220.5(a)(1). Use protected materials only for the proceeding and comply with return/disposal timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality designation categories and case-by-case determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery material may be designated as 'confidential' only if the party reasonably and in good faith believes it consists of: (i) bona fide confidential financial information not public; (ii) bona fide confidential non-obvious business plans, product development, or marketing plans not public; (iii) any truly personal or intimate information about an individual not known by the public; or (iv) any other category the Board grants leave to designate as confidential. Parties must make confidentiality determinations on a document-by-document basis and shall not designate all produced material as confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid blanket confidentiality designations; be prepared to justify confidentiality designations on a document-specific basis, and attempt to resolve disputes before seeking Board resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting confidential information — sealed filings and redactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential discovery materials or references to them may be submitted under seal or by redaction. If filed under seal, the confidential document must be accompanied by a redacted copy suitable for the public record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing confidential materials, include a public redacted version unless otherwise directed; follow Board procedures for sealed filings and attempts to resolve confidentiality disputes before Board intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board authority to remove confidentiality designations
rubrics_metrics.description: After notice and an opportunity for the designating party to respond, the Board may remove a confidentiality designation on its own initiative or upon a request from a party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect the Board to evaluate confidentiality claims and to remove designations when appropriate after notice and response opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Custom protective orders are disfavored
rubrics_metrics.description: Custom protective orders negotiated by parties are disfavored. A request for a custom order must be accompanied by a stipulation explaining the need and include the custom order as an exhibit; the Board may exercise discretion in granting such requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer the Board's standard protective order; if a custom order is necessary, provide a strong stipulation and the proposed order as an exhibit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personally identifiable information (PII) redaction requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Regardless of confidentiality designation, parties must redact social security numbers, taxpayer identification numbers, birth dates, health information protected by law, names of individuals known to be minors, and financial account numbers from any public filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure PII is redacted from public filings even if the document is otherwise confidential; file sealed versions as appropriate to preserve unredacted materials for the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violations of protective orders may be bad-faith conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations of a protective order may constitute bad-faith conduct pursuant to §232.3 of this subchapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat protective order obligations seriously to avoid sanctions or bad-faith findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence admissibility and weight
rubrics_metrics.description: All evidence that is relevant and not unduly repetitious or privileged shall be admissible. Evidence with authentication or credibility issues will have its weight discounted accordingly. The Board reserves the right to discount or not admit evidence with serious credibility issues entirely, or to request clarification from a party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare evidence with clear authentication and credibility support; expect the Board to evaluate relevance, repetitiveness, privilege, and credibility when admitting or assigning weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of witnesses at hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: All witnesses testifying at a hearing must take an oath or affirmation. Any Board member may administer oaths and ask questions of any witness; each party will have the opportunity to ask questions of each witness and other parties. The Board shall manage the hearing conduct and may limit the number of witnesses or scope of questioning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare witnesses to testify under oath, anticipate Board questioning, and be ready for limits on witness numbers or questioning scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibits at hearing — admission of submitted documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless specifically excluded by the Board or due to a Board ruling on an objection, all documents submitted through statements under §222.15 shall be deemed admitted and marked as exhibits in the same order as presented through the documentary evidence a party submitted with the party statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize documentary evidence in the order you intend it to be admitted and ensure compliance with documentary submission rules; be prepared to address objections but understand that properly submitted documents are generally deemed admitted as exhibits.
